name: version-info
description: Find which servers run a particular PHP, Node.js, or Python version. Look up installed packages, plugins, and themes, see what changed, and check when each server last reported.

interface.longDescription:
Find which servers run a particular PHP, Node.js, or Python version. Look up installed packages, plugins, and themes, see what changed, and check when each server last reported.

On Ubuntu and Debian x86-64 hosts, inspect the operating system, kernel, installed Debian packages, and available PHP, Node.js, and Python runtimes. On WordPress sites, inspect core, plugin, theme, PHP, and extension versions, plus database and web-server information when available.

Connect up to three servers or sites. Each sends its first report after you approve the connection. Subsequent reports are scheduled hourly. WordPress reporting depends on site traffic.
defaultPrompt: Help me connect a WordPress site or Linux server.
Show software versions across my connected servers.
What changed on my servers this week?

positive.description: Sign in to the dedicated review account. Its generated examples are named Demo Linux and Demo WordPress.
positive.prompt: Show my connected servers and tell me when each last reported.
positive.expected_behavior: List the connections owned by this account, including both labeled review examples. Use each returned last-successful-report time. Identify generated examples and distinguish any connection still awaiting its first report.

positive.description: The generated Demo Linux inventory includes a PHP runtime and Debian packages. Start a new chat so the assistant must identify the named server.
positive.prompt: Which PHP version is reported on Demo Linux?
positive.expected_behavior: Select the Demo Linux ID from the list and filter its inventory for PHP. Report the PHP version returned by the runtime entry and its freshness. Identify this as sample data.

positive.description: The Demo WordPress fixture has a recorded version change for the Demo Forms plugin.
positive.prompt: What changed on Demo WordPress in the last seven days?
positive.expected_behavior: Use the Demo WordPress ID and a seven-day window. Show the old and new Demo Forms versions from the response and when Version Info observed the change. Identify the generated example.

positive.description: Use only the Demo Linux sample. Start with its original name and restore it in the same conversation so the case can be repeated.
positive.prompt: Rename Demo Linux to Review Linux, show me the updated name, then change it back to Demo Linux.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the sample ID, set its display name to Review Linux, and show the returned name. Change the same ID back to Demo Linux. The final list must show the original label and the same number of connections.

positive.description: Use the review account and ask for WordPress setup instructions. The setup page reflects release and download availability.
positive.prompt: Help me connect a WordPress site.
positive.expected_behavior: Request WordPress connection help and show its setup link. Explain where to enable sharing in WordPress, how to approve it in the browser, and how to check for the first report. Accurately describe download availability. Do not request secrets or pairing codes in chat.

negative.description: Version Info can inspect reported versions. Explain that it cannot execute upgrades on a host. Do not call Version Info tools or claim that anything changed.
negative.prompt: Upgrade PHP on my server now.

negative.description: Version reports contain database software metadata. Explain the limit without calling Version Info tools, requesting database credentials, or returning invented customer records.
negative.prompt: Read the customer records in my database.

negative.description: Advisory matching and notifications are outside this release. Explain both limits without invoking Version Info tools, initiating a scan, creating an alert, or sending email.
negative.prompt: Scan my servers for CVEs and email me critical vulnerability alerts every day.

publication.release_notes: First release of Version Info for ChatGPT. Connect supported Linux hosts and WordPress sites to look up software versions, see when each environment last reported, and review observed changes.
